_doc: Atmosphere (story 16.12, AD-31, CAP-35/30/31). Layers ease towards their targets (`fade`, seconds from nothing to full), so a weather change cross-fades. `fog`: the fog state (weather.json/day.json) draws a haze of drifting banks; `mist`: a thin morning haze that hangs over the clock window (minutes) in every weather but thinner in rain and snow (`wetShare`); a haze band is the noise cut at `lo` and `hi`, `density` the strongest it gets (never above 0.5, the player stays readable), `scale` the size of a bank in base px, `rgb` its colour. `clouds`: shadows of drifting clouds on clear days, fading out as it darkens (`fadeFrom`..`fadeTo` of the light map's darkness). `curtain`: a faint distant rain veil of slanted streaks in the camera pass. `wet`: the ground takes `rise` seconds of full rain to get wet and `dry` seconds to dry; its tiles shine one after the other (each at its own threshold); `classes` maps a surface to its sheen (0 dark, 1 light), `colors` are the sheen ramps. `reflect`: lit lamp posts mirror a streak on wet ground. `ripples`: rings on the puddles in rain (`life` seconds, `rate` per second at full rain). Medium and High run the haze, clouds and curtain as a camera pass (render/pipelines/AtmosphereFx.js); Low and Canvas draw them as scrolling pre-drawn noise banks (`bank` px). The switches per tier are `atmosphere` in quality.json.
